title: Admin - Add Internal Admin - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - Add Internal Admin feature on the Y4J platform. This feature includes an 'Add Internal Admin' button that opens a modal dialog with form fields (Name, Email, Role), a permissions section, and an 'Add Admin' submit button. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for modal dialog accessibility, form accessibility, keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility, validation error handling, and dynamic content updates.

testCases.title: Add Internal Admin button has accessible name and keyboard activation
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin and navigated to the Internal Administrators page
steps: Tab to the 'Add Internal Admin' button
Verify the button has a visible focus indicator
Verify screen reader announces the button name and role
Press Enter to activate the button
Verify the modal opens
Close the modal, return focus to button, press Space to activate
Verify the modal opens again
expectedResults: Button is reachable via Tab key
Visible focus indicator appears with at least 3:1 contrast
Screen reader announces 'Add Internal Admin, button'
Enter key opens the modal
Space key also opens the modal
No mouse interaction is required
testCases.postconditions: Add Internal Admin button is fully accessible

testCases.title: Modal has proper dialog role and accessible name
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, 'Add Internal Admin' button is available
steps: Click or activate the 'Add Internal Admin' button
Verify the modal has role='dialog' or uses the <dialog> element
Verify the modal has aria-modal='true'
Verify the modal has an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing to the modal heading)
Verify screen reader announces the dialog name and role on open
expectedResults: Modal has role='dialog' or is a <dialog> element
aria-modal='true' is set on the dialog
Modal has accessible name (e.g., 'Add Internal Admin' via aria-labelledby)
Screen reader announces 'Add Internal Admin dialog' or similar when opened
Background content is marked as inert or aria-hidden='true'
testCases.postconditions: Modal is properly identified as a dialog by assistive technologies

testCases.title: Focus moves to modal on open
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, about to open the modal
steps: Activate the 'Add Internal Admin' button
Observe where keyboard focus moves when the modal opens
Verify focus is placed on the first focusable element in the modal (close button or first input)
Verify focus does not remain on the trigger button behind the modal
expectedResults: Focus moves into the modal immediately upon opening
Focus is placed on the first focusable element (e.g., close button, heading, or Name input)
Focus is not left on the background page
Screen reader announces the modal context
testCases.postconditions: Focus is properly managed when modal opens

testCases.title: Modal traps focus within the dialog
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: With the modal open, press Tab repeatedly
Verify focus cycles through all interactive elements within the modal
When focus reaches the last element, press Tab again
Verify focus wraps back to the first element in the modal
Press Shift+Tab from the first element
Verify focus wraps to the last element in the modal
Verify focus never escapes to background page elements
expectedResults: Tab cycles through: close button → Name input → Email input → Role dropdown → Permissions section → Add Admin button (and back)
Focus wraps from last to first element on Tab
Focus wraps from first to last element on Shift+Tab
Focus never reaches background page elements while modal is open
testCases.postconditions: Focus is properly trapped within the modal

testCases.title: Escape key closes the modal
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: With the modal open, press the Escape key
Verify the modal closes
Verify focus returns to the 'Add Internal Admin' button that triggered the modal
Verify no data is submitted
expectedResults: Escape key closes the modal
Focus returns to the 'Add Internal Admin' trigger button
No form data is submitted or saved
Screen reader announces the modal has closed (or context returns to page)
testCases.postconditions: Modal can be dismissed via keyboard without side effects

testCases.title: Focus returns to trigger button when modal is closed
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: Close the modal using the close button (X)
Verify focus returns to the 'Add Internal Admin' button
Open the modal again, close with Escape
Verify focus returns to the 'Add Internal Admin' button
Open the modal, submit the form successfully
Verify focus returns to an appropriate element on the page
expectedResults: After close button: focus returns to 'Add Internal Admin' button
After Escape: focus returns to 'Add Internal Admin' button
After successful submission: focus returns to trigger button or newly added admin card
Focus is never lost to the top of the page
testCases.postconditions: Focus is properly restored after modal closes

testCases.title: Name input field has accessible label
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: Navigate to the Name input field using Tab
Verify the input has a visible label 'Name' or similar
Verify the label is programmatically associated (via <label for>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby)
Verify screen reader announces the field name and type
expectedResults: Name input has a visible label
Label is programmatically associated with the input
Screen reader announces 'Name, edit text' or similar
Clicking the label focuses the input (if using <label for>)
testCases.postconditions: Name field is properly labeled for assistive technologies

testCases.title: Email input field has accessible label and autocomplete
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: Navigate to the Email input field using Tab
Verify the input has a visible label 'Email' or similar
Verify the label is programmatically associated
Check for autocomplete='email' attribute
Check for type='email' attribute
Verify screen reader announces the field name and type
expectedResults: Email input has a visible label
Label is programmatically associated with the input
Input has autocomplete='email' for autofill support
Input has type='email' for appropriate keyboard on mobile
Screen reader announces 'Email, edit text' or similar
testCases.postconditions: Email field is properly labeled and supports autofill

testCases.title: Role selection has accessible label and keyboard support
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: Tab to the Role selection control
Verify it has an accessible label (e.g., 'Role')
If dropdown: press Enter/Space to open, arrow keys to navigate options
If radio buttons: use arrow keys to move between options
Select an option using keyboard
Verify screen reader announces the selected role
expectedResults: Role control has accessible name 'Role'
Control is operable via keyboard (Enter/Space/Arrow keys)
Options include role names (Super Admin, Limited-Access Admin)
Screen reader announces the control type, name, and current value
Selected option is communicated to assistive technology
testCases.postconditions: Role selection is fully accessible via keyboard and screen reader

testCases.title: Required fields are indicated accessibly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: Observe the form fields in the modal
Check if required fields are visually indicated (asterisk, 'required' text)
Verify required fields have aria-required='true' or required attribute
Verify screen reader announces fields as required
Check that the required indicator is not conveyed by color alone
expectedResults: Required fields are visually marked (e.g., asterisk with legend or 'required' text)
Fields have aria-required='true' or HTML required attribute
Screen reader announces 'required' when focusing on mandatory fields
Required indication does not rely solely on color
testCases.postconditions: Users understand which fields are mandatory

testCases.title: Permissions section is accessible and keyboard operable
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open and Role has been selected (permissions section visible)
steps: Select a Role to make the permissions section available
Tab to the permissions section
Verify the section has a group label (e.g., fieldset/legend or role='group' with aria-label)
Navigate through individual permission controls (checkboxes/toggles)
Verify each permission has an accessible label
Toggle permissions using keyboard (Space for checkboxes)
expectedResults: Permissions section has a group label (e.g., 'Permissions' or 'Assigned Permissions')
Each permission control has an accessible name describing the permission
Checkboxes/toggles are operable via Space key
Screen reader announces checked/unchecked state
All permissions are reachable via Tab or arrow keys
testCases.postconditions: Permissions section is fully accessible

testCases.title: Permissions section appearance is announced when it becomes available
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open, Role has not been selected yet
steps: Focus on the Role selection control
Select a role (e.g., 'Super Admin')
Observe if the permissions section appears dynamically
Verify screen reader is informed of the new content availability
Check if aria-live or focus management communicates the change
expectedResults: When permissions section appears, screen reader is notified (via aria-live='polite' or focus shift)
User is not disoriented by the new content appearing
New section does not steal focus unexpectedly
If focus moves to permissions, it is intentional and helpful
testCases.postconditions: Dynamic permissions section appearance is communicated accessibly

testCases.title: Add Admin submit button has accessible name and keyboard activation
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open with form filled
steps: Tab to the 'Add Admin' button
Verify the button has a visible focus indicator
Verify screen reader announces 'Add Admin, button'
Press Enter to submit the form
Verify the form submits
Reopen modal, fill form, press Space on the button
Verify the form submits
expectedResults: Button is reachable via Tab within the modal
Visible focus indicator appears
Screen reader announces 'Add Admin, button'
Enter key submits the form
Space key also submits the form
Button is not activated by other keys
testCases.postconditions: Submit button is fully accessible

testCases.title: Empty name field validation error is accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open, Name field is empty
steps: Leave the Name field empty
Fill in Email and Role
Click/activate 'Add Admin' button
Verify an error message appears for the Name field
Verify the error is programmatically associated with the Name input (aria-describedby or aria-errormessage)
Verify screen reader announces the error
Verify focus moves to the first field with an error
expectedResults: Error message is displayed visually near the Name field
Error message is programmatically linked to the input (aria-describedby)
Input has aria-invalid='true'
Screen reader announces the error when field is focused
Focus moves to the Name field (first error)
Error message text clearly describes the issue (e.g., 'Name is required')
testCases.postconditions: Validation error for empty name is accessible

testCases.title: Invalid email format validation error is accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open
steps: Enter a valid name
Enter an invalid email format (e.g., 'notanemail')
Select a role
Click/activate 'Add Admin' button
Verify an error message appears for the Email field
Verify the error is programmatically associated with the Email input
Verify screen reader announces the error
expectedResults: Error message is displayed visually near the Email field
Error message clearly describes the issue (e.g., 'Please enter a valid email address')
Error is linked via aria-describedby or aria-errormessage
Input has aria-invalid='true'
Screen reader announces the error when Email field is focused
testCases.postconditions: Invalid email validation error is accessible

testCases.title: Duplicate email error is accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open, an admin with the same email already exists
steps: Enter a name
Enter an email that already exists in the system
Select a role and permissions
Click/activate 'Add Admin' button
Verify a duplicate email error is displayed
Verify the error is announced by screen reader
Verify the error is associated with the Email field
expectedResults: Duplicate email error message is displayed clearly
Error is announced by screen reader (via aria-live='assertive' or role='alert', or focus management)
Error is associated with the Email input field
Input has aria-invalid='true'
Error message clearly states the email is already in use
testCases.postconditions: Duplicate email error is communicated to all users

testCases.title: API failure error notification is accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open, API is configured to fail
steps: Fill in all required fields with valid data
Click/activate 'Add Admin' button (with API failure simulated)
Verify an error notification is displayed
Verify the error uses role='alert' or aria-live='assertive'
Verify screen reader immediately announces the error
Verify the error does not rely solely on color
expectedResults: Error notification is visually displayed with clear message
Screen reader immediately announces the error (role='alert' or aria-live='assertive')
Error includes text prefix or icon (not just red color)
Error text has sufficient contrast (4.5:1)
User can retry the action after the error
testCases.postconditions: API failure is communicated immediately to all users

testCases.title: Successful admin creation is announced accessibly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open with valid data
steps: Fill in all required fields with valid data
Click/activate 'Add Admin' button
Verify a success message is displayed or the modal closes
Verify screen reader announces the success
Verify the new admin appears in the list
expectedResults: Success is communicated (via toast/notification with role='status' or aria-live='polite')
Screen reader announces success (e.g., 'Admin added successfully')
Modal closes after successful creation
Focus returns to appropriate element on the page
New admin is visible in the list
testCases.postconditions: Successful creation is communicated to all users

testCases.title: Modal close button has accessible name
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: Tab to the close button (X) in the modal
Verify it has an accessible name (e.g., 'Close', 'Close dialog', not just 'X')
Verify screen reader announces the button name and role
Press Enter to close the modal
Verify the modal closes
expectedResults: Close button has accessible name (aria-label='Close' or similar, not just 'X')
Screen reader announces 'Close, button' or 'Close dialog, button'
Button is operable via Enter and Space
Modal closes when button is activated
testCases.postconditions: Close button is properly labeled and functional

testCases.title: Form fields have sufficient color contrast
testCases.componentElement: All form field text and labels in modal
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: Use a contrast checker tool
Measure contrast of field labels against modal background
Measure contrast of input text against input background
Measure contrast of placeholder text against input background
Measure contrast of error message text
Measure contrast of the 'Add Admin' button text
expectedResults: All label text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio
Input text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio
Placeholder text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio (or visible label exists)
Error message text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio
Button text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against button background
testCases.postconditions: All text in the modal is readable for users with low vision

testCases.title: Modal form is functional at 200% browser zoom
testCases.componentElement: Add Internal Admin modal at 200% zoom
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open
steps: Set browser zoom to 200%
Verify the modal is fully visible (or scrollable within viewport)
Verify all form fields are visible and usable
Verify labels are not clipped or overlapping inputs
Verify the 'Add Admin' button is accessible
Submit the form and verify error messages are visible
expectedResults: Modal content is fully accessible at 200% zoom
If modal exceeds viewport, it is scrollable
No text is clipped or hidden
Form fields and buttons remain usable
Error messages are visible without horizontal scrolling
testCases.postconditions: Modal form is fully functional at 200% zoom

testCases.title: Modal reflows correctly at 320px viewport width
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open
steps: Resize browser viewport to 320px width
Verify modal content reflows to single column
Verify all form fields are accessible without horizontal scrolling
Verify buttons are fully visible and tappable
Submit the form and verify error messages display correctly
expectedResults: Modal content reflows to fit narrow viewport
No horizontal scrollbar for form content
All fields, labels, and buttons are accessible
Error messages are visible and readable
testCases.postconditions: Modal works correctly on narrow viewports

testCases.title: Error messages do not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open, form has validation errors
steps: Submit the form with empty/invalid fields to trigger errors
Observe how errors are indicated visually
View the page in grayscale mode
Verify errors are still identifiable without color
expectedResults: Error messages include text description (not just red border)
Error icon or prefix text accompanies color indication
In grayscale mode, errors are still clearly identifiable
Error state uses multiple visual cues (text + icon + border)
testCases.postconditions: Errors are perceivable regardless of color vision

testCases.title: Error suggestions provide guidance for correction
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, modal is open, form has validation errors
steps: Submit with empty Name field - check error message
Submit with invalid email format - check error message
Submit with duplicate email - check error message
Verify each error message suggests how to fix the issue
expectedResults: Empty name error suggests: 'Please enter the administrator name' or similar
Invalid email error suggests: 'Please enter a valid email address (e.g., user@example.com)'
Duplicate email error suggests: 'This email is already associated with an admin account'
Error messages are constructive and guide the user to correct the issue
testCases.postconditions: Users receive helpful guidance to fix form errors

testCases.title: Modal background overlay prevents interaction with page behind
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add Internal Admin modal is open
steps: With the modal open, try clicking on elements behind the modal overlay
Verify background elements are not clickable
Try using screen reader to navigate to background content
Verify background content is not accessible while modal is open
expectedResults: Background elements are not clickable while modal is open
Background content has aria-hidden='true' or is inert
Screen reader cannot navigate to background content
Only modal content is interactive while modal is open
testCases.postconditions: Modal properly isolates interaction from background
